title: Break Up the Hard Ground
old_p1: Most people in Hosea’s land were farmers, so Heavenly Father used a farming word. “Break up your fallow ground,” He said.
Fallow ground is dirt that sat too long without being planted. It gets hard and crusty, and little seeds cannot grow there at all. A farmer has to dig it up and make it soft again first.
old_p2: “Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy,” He said. Sow means plant, and reap means gather. Righteousness means doing right. Plant good things, and kindness grows back.
“It is time to seek the Lord,” He said, “till He come and rain righteousness upon you.” The farmer digs, and Heavenly Father sends the rain.
Hearts can get hard, too. Tonight, feel your heart go soft, ready for good things to grow.
p1: Most people in the prophet Hosea’s land were farmers. They had stopped listening to Heavenly Father. So He used a farming picture they knew.
He said, “Break up your fallow ground.” Fallow ground is dirt nobody has planted for a long time. It gets hard, and seeds cannot grow. A farmer must dig it up to make it soft.
Heavenly Father was really talking about their hearts. Their hearts had grown hard, like that ground.
p2: He said, “Plant good things, and you will gather kindness.” He said it was time to look for Him. Then He would come and rain goodness on them, like rain on a garden.
Hearts can get hard and grumpy sometimes. Saying sorry and being kind makes a heart soft again. Tonight, pick one kind thing to plant tomorrow, like sharing.
